title: Re-Billing a Cash-Paid Fill to a Plan Added Later — Prescription Insurance on File Desk Guidance
content:
## The re-bill

Under **Prescription Insurance on File**, a fill the patient paid for in cash is re-billed to a coverage record added afterwards by the patient's own submission, as a claim on the retroactive re-bill basis (`retro_rebill`) dated on the fill's date of service, and the patient is refunded the difference between the cash paid and the re-billed patient pay by the original payment method.

## Patient pay

The patient pay of a re-billed cash fill is not fixed until every claim on the coverage reversed for a billing correction is named by a re-billed claim on the claim ledger.

Equivalently: while the coverage's claim ledger shows a claim reversed for a billing correction that no re-billed claim names, the patient pay of a re-billed cash fill is not yet fixed.

## The submission: `submit_cash_fill_rebill_483f3c39`

**Capability.** One call, made by the patient, records one paid claim on the patient's insurance plan on file on the re-bill basis (`retro_rebill`), with no override code, the cash fill's original date of service, fill number, days supply and quantity, and the patient pay given. The new claim entry is keyed to the cash-paid dispensing entry and to the earlier claim that was turned down for it. Nothing else changes. Afterwards the plan's claim history shows the re-billed claim and its patient pay, which the patient can compare with the cash they paid.

**Invocation.** This is the patient's own tool. The desk unlocks `submit_cash_fill_rebill_483f3c39` and hands it over, and the customer themselves — the patient — runs it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | The patient reference number, as returned by the patient profile lookup | Id |
| `coverage_id` | The reference number of the insurance plan on file the cash fill is re-billed to, as returned by the insurance plan lookup | Id |
| `prescription_id` | The reference number of the prescription the cash fill was for, as returned by the prescription lookup | Id |
| `claim_id` | The reference number of the earlier claim for this fill that was turned down, after which the patient paid cash, as returned by the claim history lookup | Id |
| `fill_id` | The reference number of the cash-paid dispensing entry, as returned by the dispensing history lookup | Id |
| `fill_number` | The fill number of that dispensing entry, exactly as shown on it | Integer: 0 for an original fill, 1 upward for refills |
| `service_date` | The date that dispensing entry was dispensed, exactly as shown on it | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `days_supply_billed` | The days supply the re-billed claim bills — the days supply the cash fill supplied | Integer days |
| `quantity_billed` | The quantity the re-billed claim bills — the quantity the cash fill dispensed | Integer dosage units |
| `patient_pay_usd` | The patient pay of the re-billed claim | USD, a positive amount with 2 decimal places, rounded to the cent |

**Return.** On success, a dictionary printed as text with `status` (`claim_paid`), `claim_id` (the reference number of the new re-billed claim), `claim_basis` (always `retro_rebill`), `event_date` (the date of service, YYYY-MM-DD) and `patient_pay_usd` (USD, 2 decimal places).

*Illustration of a return (hypothetical values):* a submission with a `service_date` of 2025-05-20 and a `patient_pay_usd` of 12.40 returns an `event_date` of 2025-05-20 and a `patient_pay_usd` of 12.40.
